prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1471; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a two-vehicle collision on a Houston, Texas roadway where Driver 1 was changing lanes and made contact with the side of Driver 2's vehicle. Driver 1 was operating the vehicle and was identified as the named insured on the policy. A Passenger was also present in the vehicle and was confirmed at the scene by officers and independent witnesses. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash. Based on the direction of impact and the vehicles' speeds, the reported injury appears consistent with the kind and force of this collision. Witnesses, scene photographs, and Driver 2 each gave accounts that matched the sequence of events described by Driver 1. Officers observed no indication that the vehicle had sustained prior damage, and none is known from records reviewed. Damage observed on the vehicles was visible along the side panels, but it remains unclear whether all of the damage recorded resulted from this single impact and further inspection will be needed to determine that question.
